theory.intro: Kilometres measure long distances. A kilometre is just $1000$ metres, so we can change between the two units by multiplying or dividing by $1000$.
facts: To change **metres to kilometres**, divide by $1000$.
To change **kilometres to metres**, multiply by $1000$.
steps: Decide which unit is larger (km) and which is smaller (m).
Multiply by $1000$ to go km $\to$ m; divide by $1000$ to go m $\to$ km.
Write the answer with the correct unit.

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) Write $13$ kilometres using the abbreviation, then change it to metres.
(b) Change $17000$ metres to kilometres.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $13$ kilometres $=13\text{ km}$
To change kilometres to metres, multiply by $1000$.
$13\times1000=13000$
$13\text{ km}=13000\text{ m}$
(b) To change metres to kilometres, divide by $1000$.
$17000\div1000=17$
$17000\text{ m}=17\text{ km}$

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) Write $4287$ metres as kilometres and metres.
(b) Write $8$ kilometres $63$ metres using the abbreviations, then record the whole distance in metres.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $4287\text{ m}=4000\text{ m}+287\text{ m}$
$4000\text{ m}=4\text{ km}$
So $4287\text{ m}=4\text{ km }287\text{ m}$.
(b) $8$ kilometres $63$ metres $=8\text{ km }63\text{ m}$
$8\text{ km}=8000\text{ m}$
$8000\text{ m}+63\text{ m}=8063\text{ m}$

workedExamples.question_text:
Order these distances from shortest to longest:
$5\text{ km }87\text{ m}$, $5136\text{ m}$, $4\text{ km }962\text{ m}$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Change all the distances to metres.
$5\text{ km }87\text{ m}=5000\text{ m}+87\text{ m}=5087\text{ m}$
$4\text{ km }962\text{ m}=4000\text{ m}+962\text{ m}=4962\text{ m}$
$4962<5087<5136$
From shortest to longest: $4\text{ km }962\text{ m}$, $5\text{ km }87\text{ m}$, $5136\text{ m}$.

workedExamples.question_text: A route is $6\text{ km}$ long. After $3487\text{ m}$, how many metres remain?
workedExamples.solution_text:
First change the whole distance to metres.
$6\text{ km}=6000\text{ m}$
$6000\text{ m}-3487\text{ m}=2513\text{ m}$
There are $2513\text{ m}$ left.

foundation.question_text: How many metres are in $1$ kilometre?

development.question_text: Write $6\text{ km }50\text{ m}$ entirely in metres.
Which is farther: $4\text{ km}$ or $3900\text{ m}$?
development.solution_text:
$4\text{ km}=4000\text{ m}$
$4000\text{ m}>3900\text{ m}$
$4\text{ km}$ is farther.

development.question_text:
A walking track is $1\text{ km }750\text{ m}$ long.
Record the whole distance in metres.

mastery.question_text:
A trail has two sections: $2\text{ km}$ and $650\text{ m}$.
Record the total length in metres.
Which is the longest distance: $1860\text{ m}$, $2.04\text{ km}$ or $1.98\text{ km}$?
mastery.solution_text:
$2.04\text{ km}=2040\text{ m}$
$1.98\text{ km}=1980\text{ m}$
$2040\text{ m}>1980\text{ m}>1860\text{ m}$
The longest distance is $2.04\text{ km}$.
